title: Testing GPU Numerics: Finding Numerical Differences Between NVIDIA and AMD GPUs
problem: Compiler-induced numerical differences occur when programs compiled for different GPUs produce different numerical results for identical inputs. This threatens the reliability of scientific codes being ported between NVIDIA and AMD GPUs in HPC environments.
motivation: Scientific HPC applications require numerical robustness and consistency across GPU platforms to ensure reproducible results and enable platform-agnostic code portability.
method: Varity random program generator creates thousands of test programs in CUDA and HIP with specified inputs; differential testing compares numerical outputs when programs execute on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs at equivalent compiler optimization levels; AMD's HIPIFY tool converts CUDA tests to HIP to identify conversion-induced numerical discrepancies.
key_novelty: Systematic differential testing of automatically generated random programs to characterize compiler-induced numerical differences between GPU platforms, including automatic code conversion artifacts.
contributions: Comprehensive characterization of numerical differences between NVIDIA and AMD GPU compilers across 600,000+ test cases
Identification of three sources: math library implementation differences, floating-point precision variation (FP64 vs FP32), and HIPIFY conversion-induced changes
Automated random program generation methodology for GPU numerical testing
Empirical evidence of subtle cross-platform numerical inconsistencies in production HPC scenarios

metrics.other: 600,000+ test cases analyzed; numerical differences identified across math libraries, precision levels, and HIPIFY conversions
